audit_findings.title: Federal divestiture is missing from the perimeter and may be double-counted
audit_findings.magnitude: Federal pretax income was $9.3m in FY2024, $7.3m in FY2025, and $4.0m in FY2026; OE and valuation effects are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Federal earnings remain in the historical OE series and influence the trend anchor, while $68.3m of sale proceeds remains in the cash bridge
audit_findings.evidence: On March 5, 2026, the Company closed on the sale of and divested Federal Industries ("Federal"), its display merchandising business to a third party for cash proceeds of $ 68.3 million, net of cash retained and subject to customary adjustments for net working capital, cash and indebtedness.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, not merely a possibility: the continuing-operations history contains Federal earnings, the perimeter is null, and sale proceeds are included in year-end cash. Federal's recent annual pretax income equals roughly 5%-12% of the $75.1m anchor, so capitalizing it can meaningfully overstate operating value in addition to crediting the sale consideration.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct every affected OE year on a continuing-business perimeter excluding Federal, retain the sale proceeds only in the bridge, recompute the log-trend anchor, and rerun all scenarios and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: The $64 million NCI purchase claim is treated like ordinary debt despite having no interest cost in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $64.0m, equal to $5.09 per diluted share, 35.8% of reported cash, and 5.2% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds the June 30 cash balance but places the NCI purchase obligation within context-only debt even though no corresponding interest expense reduces OE
audit_findings.evidence: At June 30, 2026, we had a $64.0 million obligation to purchase noncontrolling interest.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge error. The filing separately identifies $518.204m of funded debt and a $64.0m current purchase obligation that closed on July 2, 2026. Sheltering the latter under the equity-OE funded-debt rule leaves cash committed to the purchase attributed to common equity.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a July 2 post-close bridge using the actual cash and borrowings used. Deduct any unpaid claim or resulting cash reduction, then rerun equity value per share and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: FY2026 OE may retain the nonrecurring $57.1 million disposal gain
audit_findings.magnitude: $57.085m pretax and $49.246m after tax; amount retained in OE is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any retained gain inflates FY2026 OE and, through that observation, the log-trend anchor
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal year 2026, we recorded a gain on the sale of the Federal Industries business of $57.1 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The disposal gain is demonstrably nonrecurring and large relative to FY2026 OE of $91.1m, but the supplied record does not show the OE reconciliation needed to establish whether it was retained. The cash-flow statement reverses the pretax gain, which may have purged it if OE was derived consistently from operating cash flow, but that cannot be confirmed from the valuation summary.
audit_findings.action: Trace FY2026 OE from the filed income and cash-flow statements and identify the explicit $57.085m pretax or $49.246m after-tax reversal. If absent, remove it and rerun the trend anchor and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The OE numerator mixes parent-attributable earnings with consolidated adjustments and a redemption remeasurement
audit_findings.magnitude: $21.0m redemption remeasurement within the $23.911m FY2026 NCI attribution; total OE and valuation effects are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Ownership-basis inconsistencies enter the OE numerator, while the July purchase changes the economic earnings claim represented by common shares and also consumes $64.0m in the bridge
audit_findings.evidence: A re-measurement adjustment of $ 21.0 million was recorded for the year ended June 30, 2026 to record the noncontrolling interest as of June 30, 2026 at its estimated redemption value based on the terms of the Shareholder Agreement with the noncontrolling interest shareholder.
audit_findings.explanation: The $21.0m non-operating remeasurement is demonstrated and equals 28.0% of the $75.1m anchor. Removing that charge would increase recurring OE, while correcting any mismatch between parent earnings and consolidated cash-flow adjustments could move OE either way. The post-close ownership increase also cannot be valued coherently without simultaneously reflecting its purchase cost.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct FY2025-FY2026 OE component by component on one ownership basis, exclude the $21.0m remeasurement from recurring OE, establish a 100%-owned Narayan run rate, incorporate the $64.0m post-close payment in the bridge, and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Actual capex may understate normalized reinvestment needs
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 capex was $25.199m; 4%-5% of FY2026 sales is $35.664m-$44.580m, a $10.465m-$19.381m difference; FY2027 guidance is $45m-$55m
audit_findings.mechanism: Using unusually low actual capex increases historical OE and can raise the trend anchor above sustainable distributable earnings
audit_findings.evidence: We expect 2027 capital spending to be between $45 million and $55 million.
audit_findings.explanation: This affects numbers already used in the OE history, so it is not merely a forward-looking monitoring item. The filed spending ranges show a potentially significant gap, but they combine maintenance and growth investment; the record therefore cannot establish the normalized maintenance-capex adjustment or its materiality to value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain maintenance-versus-growth capex by business and year, reconcile it to depreciation and the asset base, calculate a supportable normalized maintenance charge, and rerun the OE series and anchor if that charge differs from actual capex.

audit_findings.title: The bridge omits an underfunded pension claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.192m combined U.S. and foreign funded deficit, equal to $1.21 per diluted share and 1.23% of the $1,233m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any pension cash requirement not already deducted in OE would reduce OE or require a debt-like bridge deduction
audit_findings.evidence: Our primary U.S. defined benefit plan is not 100% funded under ERISA rules at June 30, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: Even deducting the entire filed $15.192m deficit from the bridge would reduce base value only from $98.13 to about $96.92 per share, leaving the valuation conclusion unchanged relative to the $275.78 market price. The filing also shows that $6.846m of FY2026 defined-benefit contributions was deducted in operating cash flow and identifies $5.0m of expected FY2027 contributions, reducing the likelihood of a wholly omitted claim.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile pension expense and the $6.846m contribution adjustment within OE. If normalized funding is not captured, deduct the after-tax deficit or substitute normalized contributions, but no broader rerun is needed unless the reconciliation identifies obligations beyond the filed $15.192m deficit.
